A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of Transitive RL, including Appendices A–C. Their equations, results, and illustrations can be matched across baseline renaming and figure rearrangement.

before.justification: v1 reports original TRL evaluations on long-horizon and standard OGBench tasks, comparative experiments, and ablations, with detailed results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original evaluations and ablations, including the per-task results in Appendix B. Some borrowed baseline scores do not alter the presence of original experiments.

M1.justification: TRL’s loss, behavioral subgoal sampling, distance reweighting, policy extraction, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Appendix C.2 retains the same oracle-distillation procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three long-horizon environments and ten standard OGBench environments, using the same datasets and oracle-representation variants. No task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: SGT-DP, abbreviated SGT in displays, is renamed TDP. Appendix C.1 retains its sampled-subgoal procedure and losses in Equations (15)–(19), and its participation in Tables 1–2 is unchanged. Other comparator sets also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Training budgets, network sizes, preprocessing, and evaluation procedures are retained. Appendix C.3 still specifies one million training steps, 15 episodes per evaluation goal, and the same checkpoint-averaging protocol and exception for borrowed baselines.

E4.justification: The expectile, subgoal-distribution, and distance-reweighting ablations test the same questions with identical curves. v1’s Figure 5(a–c) becomes v2’s Figures 5–7; no analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions specify four random seeds, 95% confidence intervals in plots, and standard deviations in tables. No run-count or uncertainty-estimation practice changes are reported; the small interval-endpoint differences concern E6.

E6.justification: Figure 4 slightly raises BC’s displayed upper confidence bound and lowers the SGT/TDP and COE lower bounds. Its bar means and rankings, all scores in Tables 1–2, Figure 3, and the ablation curves remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, update equations, and Appendix A proofs are unchanged. The value–distance relation explicitly repeated before Equation (7) in v2 was already stated in Section 3 of v1.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces the first-to-scale novelty qualifier 'without planning' with 'beyond toy domains,' changing its explicit scope. The abstract’s method, recursion-complexity, and performance claims and the conclusion’s central message are retained.

C2.justification: The result interpretations and ablation explanations retain their meaning. Section 6 preserves the limitations concerning unbiased learning in stochastic environments and extension beyond goal-conditioned RL.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains the same implementation procedures, hyperparameters in Tables 3–5, and code-access information. The rewritten TDP paragraph changes terminology and attribution without disclosing a new implementation detail.

R1.justification: v2 adds Yang et al. (2022) to the offline GCRL discussion and references. It reframes the renamed baseline as a TDP family associated with Kaelbling, Dhiman, and Jurgenson, and qualifies the related-work comparison as concerning planning-free off-policy RL.

P1.justification: Localized edits revise the introduction and baseline description, clarify the value–distance connection, and replace SGT-DP terminology with TDP. Headers change from Preprint to ICLR 2026 publication status; most prose and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The three panels of v1’s Figure 5 become separate Figures 5–7 beside their corresponding discussions. Baseline labels change in Figure 4 and Tables 1, 2, and 5, with associated spacing and pagination adjustments.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity through more explicit baseline attribution, the value–distance explanation, and placement of ablation plots beside their discussion. Scientific support is essentially unchanged: the revised novelty wording receives no additional validation, and the small confidence-bound changes do not affect conclusions.
